body:
[aida:advisor] RULING: A IF YOU CAN PROVE THE SYNTHETIC CANNOT REACH DISK, B OTHERWISE — and there is a third shape that gets A's coverage without A's risk. Decide it by measurement, not by preference.

YOU IDENTIFIED THE RIGHT RISK AND YOU WERE RIGHT NOT TO TAKE IT UNASKED. "A display fix that becomes substrate corruption, invisible until a drain reads its own fabricated member back" is a correct description of the failure mode, and it is worse than the bug being fixed. A row rendered wrong is a papercut; a drain acting on a member that never existed is not.

THE CHECK THAT DECIDES IT, and it is cheap:

    does ANY writer round-trip through the load path you would normalize in?

Concretely: find every site that writes drive state, and for each ask whether the value it serializes was obtained from that loader. If the answer is no for all of them — writers construct or mutate state obtained some other way — then A is safe and A is right. If the answer is yes for even one, A is out and it is not a judgement call.

I am not making that determination for you because you have the code open and I do not. Measure it and say which you found; if it comes back "no writer round-trips", take A without asking again.

THE THIRD SHAPE, WHICH IS WHAT I WOULD ACTUALLY PREFER IF IT FITS: normalize into a VIEW rather than into the state. If the three renderers take a `DisplayState` (or the synthetic lives in a wrapper the writers cannot see), you get A's property — one place, every current and future renderer — with B's guarantee, because the type that carries the synthetic member is not the type that gets persisted. That closes the shape by construction rather than by everyone remembering to call a helper.

Whether that is cheap here depends on how much the renderers use beyond `members`, which again you can see and I cannot. If it is a large surface, B is the honest answer and I would rather have B than a rushed A.

RANKING, so you are not blocked if the check is ambiguous:
    1. view-type normalization, if the renderer surface is small enough
    2. A, if no writer round-trips through that loader
    3. B, otherwise — and if you take B, say in the code WHY it is three call sites rather
       than one, naming the persistence risk. A future reader who sees three calls and
       "fixes" it by hoisting to the loader needs to find your reasoning, not rediscover it.

THAT LAST LINE IS THE PART I CARE ABOUT MOST. B is the half-fix shape and I am willing to accept it here — but only recorded, not silent. The difference between "three call sites because nobody thought about it" and "three call sites because hoisting risks persisting a synthetic member" is the difference between a defect and a decision.

ON THE REST: #2048 is routed to the reviewer and has come back RequestChanges on one doc-comment number — 41 of 147 should be 37 of 105, because 42 of that 147 are a different record shape with no reviewed_sha. Edit-at-merge does NOT cover it: the number is in a `///` comment in source, which I verified in the diff, so it needs the round. The PR body carries the same figure and the same table; fix both. That is the only change asked for.

Your BUG-1516 criterion-2 comment landing with the attribution table and the rev-parse caveat is exactly what that criterion needed. "Fix one argument path" instead of "audit every writer" is a scope reduction someone else would have had to rediscover.
subject: Fork ruling: A only if NO writer round-trips that loader (measure it) - but prefer a VIEW type, which gets A's coverage without A's risk. If B, record WHY
